query: Why do expense decline rates differ across departments?

per_column.name: asset_category_type
per_column.rationale: Categorizing expenses into hardware/service/travel/misc gives a genuine axis to compare decline rates across departments. Values are soundly read from short_description and ci text (e.g. 'Provision of Services'->service, 'Dell Laptop'->hardware).

per_column.name: procurement_timing_signal
per_column.rationale: Timing/turnaround could plausibly relate to declines, giving useful leverage. However groundedness is weak: rows with processed_date 'nan' are still confidently labeled 'rapid_turnaround', and there is no visible opened_at-to-processed interval in samples to justify the pace distinction. The signal appears partly invented.

per_column.name: creation_origin
per_column.rationale: Manual vs auto-generated origin is a plausible axis, but the source fields shown (short_description, ci, processed_date) do not clearly indicate provenance. Every sample is labeled 'manual_entry' with no visible textual warrant, suggesting an unsupported/guessed assignment.

per_column.name: asset_specification_completeness
per_column.rationale: Whether the ci is a concrete identifier vs generic placeholder is derivable from the ci text (e.g. 'OptiPlex 7050'->complete, 'Random Access Memory Component'->generic, 'ISP Services'->service_descriptor). Modestly useful as a proxy for documentation quality that could correlate with declines, though somewhat correlated with asset_category_type.

per_column.name: expense_nature
per_column.rationale: Well grounded in the description text, but largely redundant with asset_category_type (hardware->hardware_acquisition, service->service_subscription), so it adds limited new analytical leverage beyond that column.

judge.rationale: The category-oriented columns (asset_category_type, asset_specification_completeness, expense_nature) are well grounded in the short_description/ci text and give real axes for comparing decline behavior, though expense_nature is mostly redundant with asset_category_type. The two provenance/timing columns (procurement_timing_signal, creation_origin) are analytically plausible but poorly grounded: samples show confident labels where the source text is silent or 'nan', indicating invented values. Overall the set is moderately useful with mixed groundedness.
